result:
I found one real bug in `cleo.ui.table` (Medium, Logic): `Table.set_column_max_width` sets a minimum column width instead of a maximum.

**The bug.** The method stores the width in `self._column_widths`, which is the minimum-width dict, instead of `self._column_max_widths`. Nothing ever writes to `_column_max_widths`, so the code that wraps and caps long cells never runs. In practice it does the same thing as `set_column_width`:
- `set_column_max_width(0, 3)` on a 10-character cell still renders the full 10 characters.
- `set_column_max_width(0, 10)` on the 1-character cell `"a"` pads the column out to 10.

**A second problem behind it.** When I filled `_column_max_widths` by hand, wrapping worked if the table was built with an `Output`. Built with an `IO` (for example `BufferedIO`), `render()` failed on `assert isinstance(self._io, Output)`. So fixing only the setter would leave tables built on an `IO` failing as soon as a max width is set. The patch in the report fixes both: it writes to the right dict, and it gets the formatter from `self._io.output` when it isn't given an `Output`. I haven't applied the patch.

**What passed.** I tested 6 properties; the other 5 passed:
- All rendered lines are the same width, across the default, borderless, box and box-double styles.
- The same holds when cells contain newlines.
- Every cell's text appears in the output.
- Header and footer titles don't change the line widths, on tables at least 10 characters wide.
- Cells spanning several columns keep the lines the same width.

The title test also failed on a header-only table with one empty column (4 characters wide), where the title made the top and bottom borders longer. I left that out as an extreme edge case: titles truncated correctly on realistic tables.

Files are in `runs/cleo_r2`:
- `bug_report_cleo_ui_table_2026-10-05_23-39_qzm5.md`
- `test_table_pbt.py`
